title: Rich vs. King: Why Jason Cohen sold Smart Bear for life-changing certainty
summary: Jason Cohen explains why he sold Smart Bear in 2007 despite 100% annual growth. He argues you can chase "Rich" while behaving like "King" by running a profitable, durable business, and that crossing the "Freedom Line" matters more than squeezing out a bigger exit.

principles.text: Profit is the best route to being acquired: it proves the market, sets a floor on valuation, and gives you walk-away power.
principles.quote: my attitude was (and still is) that the best way to get yourself acquired is to be profitable.

principles.text: You can only negotiate well if you don't need the deal and can happily walk away.
principles.quote: Most of all, profits mean you don't *need* to sell, which gives you the ability to walk away from a deal. You have little negotiating power in any deal unless you can happily walk away.

principles.text: Aiming for "Rich" and acting like "King" is not contradictory: sustainable, long-term businesses are exactly what get acquired.
principles.quote: although the goal was "Rich," I achieved it by behaving like the goal was "King." I don't know why people find this contradictory

principles.text: Be explicit about the exit with your team up front: hires should know the company is there to make money and may be sold.
principles.quote: even before hiring someone, I would tell them that we're here to make money, and if someone offers to buy the company someday, I'm going to sell it, and all of us will make money.

principles.text: Financial freedom is non-linear: crossing the line where savings fund your lifestyle matters far more than how far past it you go.
principles.quote: If you're crossing from left to right, it doesn't matter how far to the right you go.

principles.text: Don't gamble certain life-changing money for a chance at more (the Box Game); the 2008 crash and a stalled rival deal proved the risk real.
principles.quote: a "chance of moving even further" isn't worth giving up the certainty of that life-altering event.
